kyoto_shichimiya_honpo.gf_detail: Ask. Shichimi and sansho blends are spices (shop site); the pork buns sold at the shop are wheat (2024–26 reviews). No allergen information.
kyoto_shichimiya_honpo.vegan_detail: Ask. The spice blends are plant-based by nature but no vegan claim is sourced; the dashi packs and the chicken-oil condiment are not vegan (shop site), and the buns contain pork.
kyoto_shichimiya_honpo.hours_raw: Takeaway only — a spice shop, no seating (Tabelog). 9:30–17:30, varying with the season; open all year (Tabelog). Tastings before you buy (2017–21 reviews). Pork buns with the house shichimi, ¥500, sold from the shop (May 2026). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). Online shop and stockists (shop site). Founded in the Meireki era (shichimiya.co.jp); the recipe is described as passed down to a single heir (「一子相伝の味」). At the meeting of Sannenzaka and Gojozaka on the way to Kiyomizu-dera (shop site).
kyoto_shichimiya_honpo.notes: [Shichimi · takeaway · Kiyomizu] A spice shop at the fork of Sannenzaka and Gojozaka that has sold its own shichimi togarashi since the Meireki era — "over three hundred years", the shop says: blends heavy on sansho, chilli powders, dashi packs, and a shichimi pork bun to eat as you walk. Takeaway only. Founded in the Meireki era (shichimiya.co.jp); recipe passed to a single heir, per the shop site.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop site: 「明暦年間の創業以来」 — founded in the Meireki era, "over three hundred years" (三百有余年), the recipe kept as 「一子相伝の味」, passed down to a single heir.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the shop site: preserving a flavour passed to a single heir.

anecdotes.text: A September 2025 buyer grew up with this shop’s shichimi — the one always kept at home by the reviewer’s mother — and loves it on udon.
A May 2026 visitor ate the ¥500 pork bun with a shake of the house shichimi after visiting Kiyomizu-dera.

Dinner courses with all-you-can-drink, ¥4,500 (January 2026). Reservations until the day before (Tabelog). Dogs welcome inside, including the three private rooms upstairs (January 2024, January and November 2026). No cards or e-money; PayPay (Tabelog). 25 seats: a five-seat counter downstairs, private rooms upstairs (Tabelog; 2024 review). Down a narrow alley just east of Kawaramachi-Marutamachi (2024 review, November 2025).
kyoto_teppachi_chicken.notes: [Karaage izakaya · Kawaramachi-Marutamachi] A small alley izakaya near Kawaramachi-Marutamachi known for juicy karaage: an ¥800-odd daily lunch set with free large rice and cheap bento, and ¥4,500 all-you-can-drink courses at night. Dogs are welcome inside, even in the private rooms upstairs. Closed Thursday and Sunday; PayPay or cash.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviews: an izakaya opened 9 January 2023 near Kawaramachi-Marutamachi, serving chicken dishes, lunch sets and bento.

anecdotes.text: A January 2026 family chose it for a daughter’s twentieth-birthday dinner because the dog could come inside, and had the ¥4,500 course in a private room upstairs.
A November 2025 lunch diner had the ¥800 set of karaage and stir-fried chicken with eggplant, with a free large rice.

kyoto_geijutsu_kissa_itoyufu.gf_detail: Ask. The matcha tiramisu is described as gluten-free (March 2026); the baked cheesecake and seasonal sweets are not. No cross-contact information.
kyoto_geijutsu_kissa_itoyufu.vegan_detail: Some vegan options: the matcha tiramisu is described as vegan (March 2026); ask about plant milk for lattes. The baked cheesecake is not vegan.
kyoto_geijutsu_kissa_itoyufu.hours_raw: Daily except Tuesday 7:30–18:00 (Tabelog). 「各自ワンドリンクオーダー必須キャッシュレスオンリー（現金払い不可）」 — one drink per person, and cashless only, no cash (Tabelog). A counter and benches beside a small gallery with changing exhibitions (March and April 2026). Closed 8–30 June 2026 for renovation (May 2026). In a renovated wooden townhouse that was a tobacco shop, near Higashi Honganji and Shoseien, about ten minutes from Kyoto Station; opened 2 February 2026 (Tabelog; February and April 2026).
kyoto_geijutsu_kissa_itoyufu.notes: [Gallery café · near Higashi Honganji] A quiet gallery café opened in 2026 by the Kyoto pottery brand QUTOTEN. in an old tobacco shop near Higashi Honganji: matcha lattes and coffee in its own tea ware, a vegan, gluten-free matcha tiramisu, baked cheesecake and seasonal sweets, with art and bonsai on show. Cashless only; one drink each; closed Tuesday.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviews: a gallery café produced by the Kyoto pottery brand QUTOTEN., opened 2 February 2026 in a renovated wooden former tobacco shop; the name refers to spider threads shimmering in the air (February 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Matcha latte in house tea ware; matcha tiramisu.

anecdotes.text: A March 2026 visitor watched the unsweetened matcha latte made to order and noted the small matcha tiramisu is vegan and gluten-free.
A March 2026 guest came for an exhibition of bonsai-like works and had a matcha latte in a QUTOTEN. collaboration cup.

kyoto_yakiniku_kihara_nijo.notes: [Yakiniku · north of Nijo, charcoal and tatami] A long-running, affordable charcoal yakiniku near Karasuma-Marutamachi with tatami rooms for groups: busy office-worker lunch sets of outside skirt, fresh offal and misuji at night, half-size cold noodles, courses from ¥3,850. kyoto_challe_gosho.notes: [Café · by the Imperial Palace park, crullers and tacos] A small café near the Imperial Palace park from the team behind loose kyoto and HOO: rice-flour French crullers, crisp churros with chocolate sauce, little tacos made to order and a morning plate from 9:00, with good coffee and freshly whisked matcha lattes. Open daily. Flagged: sister of loose kyoto and HOO (both in our data).

chef_bio.background: Reviewers describe CHALLE as the newest sister café of the Kyoto donut cafés loose kyoto and HOO (April and July 2026). Opened July 2024 (Tabelog). No operator was found.

kyoto_8blackbirds_cafe_shichijo.notes: [Coffee roaster café · Kawaramachi-Shichijo, from 7:30] A calm, stylish roaster café with a bird logo between Kyoto Station and Shichijo: single-origin coffee of the day, a crisp croque monsieur for breakfast, cookies and cheesecake, counter seats with power outlets, and beans to take home. kyoto_osoba_kyoshimi_nijojo.notes: [Soba · Oike near Nijo Castle, lunch only] A dignified old neighbourhood soba shop behind a green noren on the way to Nijo Castle: freshly fried tempura soba, zaru soba, curry soba and rice-bowl sets in a rich dashi, with an English menu. kyoto_royal_kitchen_bar.notes: [Curry · Horikawa-Ayanokoji, a curry house with a stage] A lively Nepali-Indian curry restaurant and bar with a stage and chandelier, popular with Indian diners: lunch sets with naan, curry and chicken tikka from about ¥1,080, open all day to 10:30 pm. Medium spice is properly spicy.

chef_bio.background: Reviewers (2026) describe a former-venue interior with a stage, chandelier and bar counter, many Indian customers and, one evening, dancing (February 2026). Only four reviews so far; one June 2026 diner found the cheese naan small. Whether it belongs to a group is not stated.

kyoto_somewhere_bar.notes: [Music bar · Teramachi-Marutamachi, gin and good records from 4 pm] A relaxed upstairs bar with a window on Marutamachi: house gins and tonics, clever little snacks, and a carefully chosen soundtrack through five Bose speakers. About ¥2,000–4,000. No cards. Closed Thursday.

chef_bio.background: An October 2025 reviewer praises the owner's selection of Japanese and international chill songs, the sound from five Bose speakers and the focus on distilled spirits. Only three reviews so far.

kyoto_kashiwaya_mitsusada.hours_raw: TAKEAWAY ONLY — a wagashi shop with no seating listed (Tabelog). 10:00–18:00 Monday–Saturday; closed Sunday (Tabelog; hours also mapple). Cash only (Tabelog). Gyoja-mochi is sold only once a year, on 16 July during the Gion Festival — about 8,000 pieces; a July 2025 reviewer reports in-person sales only since 2016 (mapple still mentions booking by 16 July — check), with a queue of 80-plus from early morning and an early opening (July 2025 reviews). Higashiyama-Yasui, by the Higashiyama-Yasui bus stop (co-trip).
kyoto_kashiwaya_mitsusada.notes: [Wagashi · Higashiyama-Yasui, takeaway only] A family wagashi house since 1806 whose 行者餅 — rice cake with white miso and sansho — is sold just once a year on 16 July for the Gion Festival, drawing a dawn queue. All year: おゝきに agar sweets from the 11th-generation head, and 音羽山. Cash only; closed Sunday.

roles: Head of the house, 11th generation (co-trip; Waraku)
chef_bio.background: A Kyoto wagashi house founded in 1806 (Waraku). Waraku describes the 10th generation as still a working confectioner in the mid-80s at the time of writing, and describes おゝきに as a family effort: the 11th-generation head reworked the 9th generation’s summer agar sweet for tea ceremonies, 京氷室 (Kyo-himuro), and the 10th set the concept. co-trip also credits おゝきに to the 11th generation. A July 2025 reviewer retells the 1806 origin of 行者餅, made during an epidemic and offered to En-no-Gyoja, and about 8,000 sold on its one day a year.
chef_bio.philosophy: “The method is a secret (laughs). The hint is air-in chocolate.” — the 10th generation on おゝきに (Waraku).
chef_bio.specialty: 行者餅 (once a year); おゝきに.

anecdotes.text: A July 2025 visitor took two days off to queue from 8:40 am for the once-a-year gyoja-mochi.
A July 2026 first-timer found the sansho, then the white miso, inside the rice cake a surprise.

chef_bio.background: A breakfast specialist in a traditional house with a garden view (November 2024 and February 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: A November 2024 couple on a morning stroll near family home found it newly opened and chose salmon yukke and grilled mackerel.
A February 2026 visitor arriving at opening on a long weekend waited about 30 minutes without a booking.

kyoto_beer_pub_takumiya.notes: [Craft beer · Karasuma-Oike] The brewery-run pub of KYOTO NUDE BREWERY near Karasuma-Oike, with about nine taps, homemade sausages, rock oysters and even dim sum; staff explain each beer. About ¥2,000–7,000.

chef_bio.background: Opened 10 March 2015 (Tabelog); the directly run outlet of KYOTO NUDE BREWERY (March 2026 review). A young, knowledgeable manager (August 2025 review). Canned beer is sold at another shop on the main street (November 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: A September 2025 visitor from Chiba on a third trip tried every fresh-hop beer and found the IPA gentle in bitterness.
A June 2026 drinker started at 4 pm with fresh rock oysters and the NUDE IPA.

cultural_comfort.note: Staff explain each beer (July 2026 review).

kyoto_kyo_gateau_the_marie.gf_detail: Reviews say all the cakes are gluten-free, made without wheat, using rice flour (August and September 2025; December 2025); confirm cross-contact with the shop.
kyoto_kyo_gateau_the_marie.vegan_detail: Ask. The cakes use soy-milk cream butter (December 2025 review; September 2023 review), but eggs are not ruled out.
kyoto_kyo_gateau_the_marie.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 12:00–21:00; closed Wednesdays; hours may change (Tabelog). Mainly take-out, with eat-in since July 2023 (July and September 2023 reviews). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). Down an alley through the gate of 京薬膳なつめ, at the same address (August 2025 review; Tabelog). 10 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae (November 2023 review).
kyoto_kyo_gateau_the_marie.notes: [Gluten-free cakes · Fuyacho-Nijo] A hidden alley cake shop of temari-ball cream puffs and chiffons, all made with rice flour and soy-milk cream butter — reviewers report every cake is gluten-free. Mostly take-out; under ¥1,000.

chef_bio.background: Opened 8 April 2023 (Tabelog); desserts inspired by temari balls, from gentle ingredients such as rice flour and soy-milk cream butter (September 2023 review); shown on Kansai TV (November 2023 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Temari cream puffs; rice-flour roll cakes.

anecdotes.text: An August 2025 parent whose child avoids animal-based cream watched the child happily finish a cream puff and try the cake too.
A September 2025 visitor, delighted that every cake was wheat-free, bought a fruit chiffon and a Shine Muscat roll.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 京gateau the marie、スイーツ・ケーキ、中京区布袋屋町520-3、月・火・木〜日 12:00〜21:00、水曜休み、カード・電子マネー・QR 可、2023年4月8日オープン。口コミ (2023〜2025年、英語): 京薬膳なつめの門をくぐった路地の奥、手まりのシュークリーム、米粉と豆乳クリームバターのケーキ、全部グルテンフリー (2025年8月・9月)、フルーツのシフォン620円、シャインマスカットのロール760円、持ち帰り中心、2023年7月からイートインも。

kyoto_yomogi_sokyudo_nijo.gf_detail: Ask. Mochi and daifuku with bean paste (2025–26 reviews); a daily bento with nikujaga (June 2026).
kyoto_yomogi_sokyudo_nijo.vegan_detail: Ask. Mochi and bean-paste sweets may suit; the bento includes meat and egg (June 2026 review).
kyoto_yomogi_sokyudo_nijo.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 10:00–17:00; closed Wednesdays; hours may change (Tabelog). No cards or QR (Tabelog). 12 seats at tables, plus two outside in summer; non-smoking (Tabelog). Take-out wagashi and eat-in with drinks (February 2026 review). About 500 m from Sanjo Keihan (Tabelog).
kyoto_yomogi_sokyudo_nijo.notes: [Wagashi café · Sakyo] A small wagashi shop with a twelve-seat café: strawberry daifuku and kusa mochi to take away or eat in with tea, chilled ame in summer and a homestyle daily bento. Under ¥1,500; cash only.

chef_bio.background: Opened 24 September 2014 (Tabelog) as the Nijo shop of 双鳩堂.

anecdotes.text: A June 2026 regular comes as much for the daily bento as for the sweets — nikujaga that day, with eggs and salads.
A January 2025 museum-goer from Okazaki Park picked up sakura mochi and strawberry daifuku to eat at the hotel.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: よもぎ 双鳩堂二条店、和菓子・甘味処・カフェ、左京区吉永町271-1、三条京阪駅から505m、月・火・木〜日 10:00〜17:00、水曜休み、カード・QR 不可、12席、禁煙、2014年9月24日オープン。口コミ (2025〜2026年、英語): いちご大福、草餅、桜餅 (240〜320円ほど)、そば茶450円、冷やしあめ、日替わりの弁当 (肉じゃがなど)。

cultural_comfort.note: Cash only (Tabelog).

kyoto_sobadokoro_miyako_nishinotoin.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: soba (with wheat flour, usually) and udon; tempura (2026 reviews) — ask about 100% buckwheat.
kyoto_sobadokoro_miyako_nishinotoin.vegan_detail: Not vegan: dashi broth, tamago-don, tempura (2026 reviews).

Queues at lunch; can sell out after 2 pm (May 2026 review). PayPay; no cards or e-money (Tabelog). 22 seats at tables; no smoking 11:00–14:00 (Tabelog). On Nishinotoin south of Takoyakushi, 5 min from Shijo or Karasuma (Tabelog).
kyoto_sobadokoro_miyako_nishinotoin.notes: [Soba · Nishinotoin] A tidy, family-run soba shop near Shijo-Karasuma with lunchtime queues: elegant pale soba with a seasonal sesame dipping sauce, a soft tamago-don and a delicate dashi. About ¥1,000–2,000.

chef_bio.background: A family-run soba shop (July 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: A May 2026 diner, defeated by queues and sold-out signs for two years, finally got in at 11:50 for the daily special.
An April 2026 regular found the small tamago-don just like the one from the now-closed Owariya.

cultural_comfort.note: Queue at lunch; PayPay or cash.

kyoto_kissa_donguri_marutamachi.gf_detail: Ask. Caramel pudding and coffee may suit; toasts, French toast, cakes and lunch dishes contain wheat (2024–2026 reviews). No gluten information.
kyoto_kissa_donguri_marutamachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan for food: pudding, cakes and toast use egg, dairy or butter; black coffee is fine (2024–2026 reviews).
kyoto_kissa_donguri_marutamachi.hours_raw: Monday–Wednesday 8:00–19:00; Thursday and Friday 8:00–17:00; closed Saturday and Sunday; hours may change (Tabelog). Tabelog also mentions a café-bar time on Thursday and Friday nights and at weekends, when smoking is not allowed, but gives no hours for it, so it is not in the hours. No reservations (Tabelog). Cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). 22 seats: an 8-seat counter like a bar and 14 at tables; smoking allowed outside café-bar time (Tabelog; February 2025). Building HANA 1F, a minute from Marutamachi Stn. Opened 2012 (February 2025 review).
kyoto_kissa_donguri_marutamachi.notes: [Kissa · Karasuma-Marutamachi, cash only] A hidden, dim, bar-style coffee shop with a long counter, run by one quiet master: smooth coffee with caramel pudding in a coffee cup, rum gâteau chocolat or French toast, and a daily lunch set. Smoking allowed. Closed weekends.

chef_bio.background: Per reviewers: a stylish café run quietly by a single master, opened in 2012 in front of Marutamachi Station, with a long bar-like counter, jazz and a dim interior (September 2024; February 2025).

anecdotes.text: A May 2024 visitor came specially for the caramel pudding served in a coffee cup.
A January 2026 business traveller stepped in and found the mood quiet and relaxing, with carefully made coffee.
A July 2026 lunch guest found it nearly full after 1 p.m. and had the daily tenshin-han with salad and iced coffee.

kyoto_natural_bal_meat_up.gf_detail: Ask. Venison steak and stewed tendon may suit, but burgers, pizza, crêpes, fries and sauces may contain wheat (2025–2026 reviews). No gluten information.
kyoto_natural_bal_meat_up.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a venison and game specialist (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_natural_bal_meat_up.hours_raw: Thursday–Tuesday and holidays 12:00–21:00 (last order 20:30); closed Wednesday (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; all-you-can-drink party plans (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), IC cards and QR (Tabelog). 30 seats: 5 at the counter, 25 at tables, plus a terrace with a smoking area; wheelchair accessible; free Wi-Fi; projector (Tabelog). Hotel Material 1F near Awata Shrine, about 5 min walk from Higashiyama Stn (Tabelog; March 2026).
kyoto_natural_bal_meat_up.notes: [Venison bar · near Awata Shrine] A bright bar in a small hotel where the staff are hunters: tender, ungamey venison steaks, burgers, curry and sausages, venison ham and jerky, with craft beer. Open from noon; closed Wednesday.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviewers: a natural-style bar specialising in venison, run by a Kyoto business that handles everything from hunting to sale; all the staff are hunters, and the young cook goes hunting himself (October 2025–February 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: Healthy dishes of game, natural ingredients and fresh vegetables; culled wild animals treated as a blessing (Tabelog; October 2025).

anecdotes.text: An October 2025 visitor after the Hello Kitty exhibition at the Kyocera Museum had fresh venison in a cosy, ten-seat-feeling room.
A November 2025 diner expected little from a young cook, then learned the cook hunts too — the steak was bright red and juicy.
A February 2026 guest was surprised that the stewed venison tendon with konnyaku had no gamey taste at all.

kyoto_more_cafe_jingu_marutamachi.gf_detail: Ask. Plate lunches of chicken, five-grain rice and vegetables and the homemade soups may suit, but dressings and cakes are not described for gluten (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_more_cafe_jingu_marutamachi.vegan_detail: Ask. The seasonal soup lunch (e.g. a pumpkin or cabbage potage) and vegetable-heavy plates may be adaptable; mains are chicken (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_more_cafe_jingu_marutamachi.hours_raw: Monday–Saturday 11:30–18:00; closed Sunday; hours may change (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; a short queue at 11:30 on some weekdays (Tabelog; October 2025). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners) and QR; no e-money (Tabelog). 22 seats incl. counter, sofas and semi- and fully private rooms; non-smoking; free Wi-Fi and some power outlets; English menu; take-out (Tabelog). Children, babies and strollers welcome, STOKKE high chairs (Tabelog; October 2026). Excel Jingu 1F, 1 min walk from Jingu-Marutamachi Stn exit 4 (Tabelog). Opened 2 August 2013 (Tabelog).
kyoto_more_cafe_jingu_marutamachi.notes: [Café · Jingu-Marutamachi] A calm, stylish café by the Kamo River, very welcoming to families: wholesome plate lunches of chicken, five-grain rice and lots of vegetables, seasonal homemade soups, Basque cheesecake and good coffee. Arrive at opening. Closed Sunday.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviewers: a café opened 2 August 2013 by Jingu-Marutamachi station, known for gently seasoned, vegetable-rich plate lunches and a welcome for children, with high chairs and room for strollers (2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: An October 2025 diner arrived ten minutes before opening to find three people already queuing.
A June 2026 parent could bring the stroller inside, and paired a Japanese-style chicken plate with Basque cheesecake.
An October 2026 regular calls it a rare café for good coffee and sweets with children, handy after a picnic by the river.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: カフェ・ケーキ、左京区下堤町77 エクセル神宮 1F、京阪神宮丸太町駅4番出口から徒歩1分、月〜土 11:30〜18:00、日曜休み、予約可、カード (JCB・AMEX・Diners)・QR 可、電子マネー不可、22席、半個室と個室、禁煙、Wi-Fi、一部の席に電源、英語のメニュー、テイクアウト、子ども・ベビーカー可、子ども用の椅子、2013年8月2日開店。口コミ (2025年3月〜2026年10月、英語): 野菜たっぷりのプレートランチ (はちみつマスタードチキン、和風マスタードチキン、塩レモンチキン、トマトソースのチキン)、五穀米、かぼちゃのドレッシング、季節の手作りスープランチ1,100円 (春キャベツと新玉ねぎのポタージュ)、かぼちゃのスープのセット、バスクチーズケーキ、コーヒーと日替わりのお茶、STOKKE の子ども用の椅子、開店前に行列も。

cultural_comfort.note: English menu; child-friendly; cards and QR.

existence.note: Tabelog listing; reviews through October 2026.

kyoto_bogota_horikawa.gf_detail: Not GF for food: toast, egg sandwiches and morning sets; coffee itself is fine (2022–2025 reviews).
kyoto_bogota_horikawa.vegan_detail: Ask. Black siphon coffee is plant-based; morning sets include egg and ham; café au lait uses milk (2023–2025 reviews).
kyoto_bogota_horikawa.hours_raw: Monday–Saturday 7:00–15:00; Sunday 8:00–15:00; hours may change (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). Cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Non-smoking now (Tabelog; November 2021). Menu in three languages (July 2025). On the south-east corner of Horikawa and Rokkaku; about 10 min walk north of Hankyu Omiya (November 2021; February 2025).
kyoto_bogota_horikawa.notes: [Kissa · Horikawa-Rokkaku, from 7:00] A nostalgic Showa coffee shop on a busy corner: siphon coffee, cappuccino with a cinnamon stick, and good-value morning sets of egg sandwiches or ham and eggs, now popular with overseas visitors too. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Per reviewers: a long-standing neighbourhood café with a retro Showa interior, brewing siphon coffee, run by an older couple with two more staff (November 2022), drawing local families and early-rising travellers (2021–2025 reviews).

anecdotes.text: A November 2021 regular found the siphon coffee as deep as ever, though now non-smoking.
An October 2025 couple on day two in Kyoto found it on Google Maps because it opens at 7 a.m.
A December 2025 visitor who had long seen it from the bus finally came in for the lettuce pilaf among local families.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 喫茶店・カフェ、中京区東堀川通六角下る壷屋町240、月〜土 7:00〜15:00、日 8:00〜15:00、予約不可、カード・電子マネー・QR 不可、禁煙。口コミ (2021年11月〜2025年12月、英語): 堀川通と六角通の南東の角、昭和レトロの店内、サイフォンのコーヒー、カフェオレ、シナモンスティックのカプチーノ、卵サンドやハムエッグのモーニング、レタスピラフ、年配の夫婦とスタッフ2人 (2022年11月)、3か国語のメニュー、海外の客や地元の家族。

kyoto_otokomae_shokudo_nanajo.notes: [Sushi izakaya · Kyoto Station, cheap nigiri from 3 pm] A big, newly refitted seafood izakaya near the station: nigiri from about ¥250, a ten-kind sashimi platter for ¥1,699, crisp eggplant gyoza and sake, from mid-afternoon to midnight. The four reviews so far read promotionally.

kyoto_higashi_honganji_osai.gf_detail: Ask when booking. A Buddhist vegetarian meal with simmered yuba and vegetables (likely soy-seasoned) and yuba tempura (February 2024); no gluten information.
kyoto_higashi_honganji_osai.vegan_detail: Ask — very promising. Tabelog lists vegan and vegetarian options; a June 2025 diner says no animal products were used and the clear soup was made with shiitake rather than an animal dashi. Confirm when booking.
kyoto_higashi_honganji_osai.hours_raw: Tabelog: by advance reservation only — book at least four days ahead; changes in numbers after that and same-day cancellations incur fees. A lunch of shojin-style "O-sai" about ¥4,000 (2024–2026). Served at tables with chairs, usually in the Shiroshoin, a hall not normally open to the public, reached through private corridors past the Noh stage; the venue can change with events and numbers (June 2025). Words of thanks are recited before and after the meal. 110 seats. Non-smoking. Cards; no e-money or QR codes. Parking, first come first served. At Higashi Hongan-ji on Karasuma-dori north of Shichijo, 5 min from Gojo Station exit 8.
kyoto_higashi_honganji_osai.notes: [Shojin · Higashi Hongan-ji, a temple meal in a private hall] Book ahead for the temple's own vegetarian "O-sai" lunch (about ¥4,000): a monk leads you through closed corridors to the Shiroshoin, where yuba, seasonal vegetables and rice are served at tables, with words of thanks before and after. Tabelog lists vegan options. Reservations at least four days ahead.

chef_bio.background: A Jodo Shinshu temple (February 2025 review). Reviewers explain that the meal follows the custom of "O-sai", food shared by people gathered for memorial services and lectures, and that a monk guides diners to the hall and explains the route (February 2024; February 2025). Guests have come after memorial services (September 2026). The temple square also hosts a monthly night market (January 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: A meal of gratitude, with words recited before and after eating (2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: June 2025: "Since no animal products were used, I was able to appreciate the flavors of the ingredients as I ate. The clear soup seemed to be made with shiitake mushrooms instead of animal-based dashi."
February 2024: "After completing the check-in, a monk guided me through a long corridor to my dining room, providing explanations along the way."
March 2024: "A reservation is required in advance, and the price is JPY 4000. You will be dining in the exclusive Shiroshoin, which is usually not open to the public."

A June 2026 traveller looking for a night café between Shichijo and Kyoto Station found it open around 6 p.m.

kyoto_gosho_delino.notes: [Italian · east of the Imperial Palace] A calm, modern machiya Italian from the team behind Lino: lunch of appetisers and a choice of monthly pastas, and dinner courses ending in roast beef and pistachio tiramisu, with Italian wines. Closed Thursday.

A July 2026 host brought a visiting French couple, drawn by the idea of tradition meeting modernity.

A dim, unmarked front you can’t see into, in a residential stretch of Gokomachi-dori just above Takeyamachi (2024–25 reviews).
kyoto_tamura_yoshitaka.notes: [Yakitori · Gokomachi-Takeyamachi] A long-running hidden yakitori counter in a residential lane near Marutamachi, behind a door you can’t see through: chicken sashimi, a sashimi platter and skewers of many cuts, from a friendly chef. Open to midnight; closed Monday.

chef_bio.background: Per reviews: a yakitori izakaya on Gokomachi-dori known to regulars for over twenty years (2013 review).

anecdotes.text: A February 2025 first-timer found it a hidden gem in a residential area, with fresh chicken sashimi, many unfamiliar cuts on skewers and a friendly chef.

kyoto_etra_shogoin.vegan_detail: Not vegan: French toast with bacon and eggs, cream puffs, cakes (2025–26 reviews). A caffeine-free chai and teas are the plant-based choices to ask about.
kyoto_etra_shogoin.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Sat, Sun 9:00–17:00; Friday 9:00–16:00; closed Wednesday and Thursday (Tabelog). Breakfast plates in the morning and a soup-and-bread lunch set; lunch can end before closing (May and July 2026). Coffee refills ¥350 (July 2026). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). A small glass-walled room with a greenhouse-like terrace and plants; people work here (December 2025, February 2026). Run by its owner alone (October 2025). Along the Lake Biwa Canal near the red-brick power station, about ten minutes from Jingu-Marutamachi (October and November 2025).
kyoto_etra_shogoin.notes: [French café · Lake Biwa Canal] A small glass-walled café by the canal near Okazaki, run single-handed by an owner who trained in France: crisp caramelised French toast and waffles for breakfast, chouquettes and choux with dips, canelés and carrot cake, and soup-and-bread lunches. Closed Wednesday and Thursday.

roles: Owner (unnamed), trained in France, who runs the café alone (October 2025)
chef_bio.background: Per reviews: a café opened in Kyoto by an owner who trained in France, serving French pastries, breakfast plates and lunch (October 2025, March 2026).

On Kiyomizu-zaka, about ten minutes from the Kiyomizu-michi bus stop (July 2026). Opened 28 April 2023 (Tabelog).
kyoto_gokago_kiyomizu.notes: [Matcha stand · Kiyomizu-zaka] A busy matcha stand on the slope up to Kiyomizu-dera where each cup of Uji matcha or hojicha is measured and whisked to order in front of you: rich matcha lattes, matcha ice cream and matcha donuts, mostly to take away. Expect a queue.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviews: a Uji matcha tea stand on Kiyomizu-zaka, opened 28 April 2023.

anecdotes.text: A March 2026 visitor watched the staff measure and whisk matcha for each group — slow, but worth it for matcha lovers.
A July 2026 visitor on the way to Kiyomizu-dera had a ¥700 matcha latte, matcha ice cream and a matcha donut.

kyoto_ichireien_tea.notes: [Tea house · Marutamachi] A calm, white family-run tea room near Marutamachi devoted to Japanese black tea: pots of Ureshino or Nansatsuma first flush and classic Indian teas in Noritake cups, scones with clotted cream and honey, a vegetable-led lunch, and food with sake in the evening. Closed Tuesday and Friday.

chef_bio.background: Per reviews: a family-run tea specialist focused on Japanese black tea, a café by day and a dining spot with sake in the evening (2024 review, January 2026).

anecdotes.text: A February 2026 visitor, sent here when the planned coffee shop was shut, tried Nansatsuma first flush, a Ceylon and mini scones, each tea brought in a pot at its peak.
A January 2026 evening guest found the café turned into a dining spot, praised the sake, and left with scones as a parting gift.

kyoto_bistro_yamagata.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a French bistro built on seafood, wagyu and game such as bear and boar (official site).

Game is delivered irregularly — call ahead to ask; the bear hot-pot and lobster courses need booking (official site). Cards (VISA, Master) (Tabelog). Shoes off at the entrance: 8–10 counter seats on the ground floor, about 20 seats at sunken tables upstairs (official site). In a narrow alley off Nishikikoji, east of Muromachi, about 2 minutes from Shijo station Exit 22 (official site; reviews). Designated smoking area (Tabelog).
kyoto_bistro_yamagata.notes: [French · alley off Nishikikoji, a veteran’s bistro with game] A shoes-off townhouse bistro where a chef of 40 years cooks at the counter: seasonal French courses ending in curry or hayashi rice, live lobster, and game — bear hot pot, boar, even badger. Lunch from about ¥1,300. Closed Sunday.

chef_bio.background: A veteran chef of about 40 years in the trade (May 2025 review) who still cooks at the counter; a September 2025 reviewer saw the same chef working seven or eight years earlier. The restaurant buys game from hunters it contracts with, and buys bear whole, direct from matagi hunters (official site).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fresh seafood, vegetables and game, chosen at home and abroad, cooked as French food that lets the seasonal ingredients speak (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Bear hot pot; seasonal courses ending in curry or hayashi rice.

anecdotes.text: In November 2024 the game hamburger was bear and Japanese badger; the server first checked the diner was fine with a strong game flavour.
A July 2025 regular came back on Yoiyama night of the Gion Festival for the omakase course.
An August 2026 lunch guest noticed a suit cover hanging on the wall as a sign of the care taken.

kyoto_imobo_hiranoya_honke.notes: [Kyoto cuisine · Maruyama Park, a family recipe for some 300 years] The house that created imobo — ebi-imo taro simmered a day and a night with dried cod — kept by one heir per generation since the mid-Edo founder. Gozen sets from ¥3,300 in a sukiya house in Maruyama Park; no service charge.

chef_bio.background: The official site traces imobo to the Hirano house’s first-generation founder, who served the prince-abbot of Shoren-in in the Genroku–Kyoho era, grew the taro that became ebi-imo in Maruyama, and cooked it with dried cod. The method, called meoto-daki, has passed by oral tradition to one heir per generation for about 300 years: from the 11th generation, revered as the house’s restorer, to the 14th (current) and a named 15th. Yoshikawa Eiji and Kawabata Yasunari wrote in its praise, and Matsumoto Seicho set a novel here (official site). A member of the Kyoto cuisine association, among others (official site).
chef_bio.philosophy: To keep the genuine taste of imobo, taught to the heir alone (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Imobo: ebi-imo and dried cod, simmered a full day and night.

anecdotes.text: A January 2025 diner noted that the Hirano family has both a Honke and a Honten near Maruyama Park, and chose the Honke.

kyoto_sanjo_inokuma_oohashi.notes: [Izakaya · Sanjo-Inokuma alley, open late] A hidden Showa-era townhouse izakaya down a narrow alley near Shijo-Omiya, open till 2:00: a handwritten daily menu of seasonal fish, oden, charcoal yakitori, fig tempura and a “little of everything” plate, with big sours and sake. anecdotes.text: An October 2026 newcomer to Kyoto treated three old friends here and urged the group to order the Manganji peppers.

kyoto_premier_bar_shichijo.notes: [Gin bar · near Kyoto Station, since 2013] A moody, roomy second-floor bar near Kyoto Station, open till 2:00, specialising in gin — dozens of aromatic bottles for G&Ts, bucks and sodas — with whisky and rum too, and a young, chatty owner happy to pick for you. 10% service charge.

chef_bio.background: A September 2026 reviewer says the bar has been open since 2013 and describes a young, talkative owner. No operator was found; 18 PREMIER BAR in Kiyamachi is a different bar.

anecdotes.text: An October 2026 guest stopping for “just one more” ended up letting the bartender choose, and discovered Diplomatico rum.

kyoto_kappou_iimura_shichijo.gf_detail: Ask. Daily lunch sets (kara-age, cutlets, croquettes, eel bowl with cold udon) and kappo courses at night; no gluten information (2026 reviews).

kyoto_kappou_iimura_shichijo.notes: [Kappo · Shichijo near Kyoto Station, ¥900 lunch] A small kappo east of Shichijo-Karasuma where people queue for the ¥900 daily lunch — one set, no ordering, carefully cooked rice — and come back at night for unshowy omakase courses around ¥8,000. chef_bio.background: A June 2026 reviewer describes the head chef and proprietress welcoming guests, with a young staff member announcing the opening. No operator was found.

anecdotes.text: A June 2026 visitor returned for lunch on a business trip because this was where a solo 50th-birthday lunch had been eaten two years earlier.
An October 2026 regular was greeted with the news that the new-crop rice had arrived, and found it tasted all the better.

kyoto_subs_sandwich_store.notes: [Sandwiches · Kawaramachi-Nijo] A five-seat American sandwich counter in a big Kyoto machiya, run by a former Kyoto-vegetable farmer: Philly cheesesteak, a teppan-grilled steak sub, homemade bacon and jam, and good coffee; takeaway too.

chef_bio.background: The owner used to farm Kyoto vegetables and makes the bacon and berry jam in house (August 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: An October 2025 diner listened to a large piece of beef sizzling on the teppan in the wooden interior before it was sliced into the sub.
An August 2026 visitor noted a local cat sometimes lounging in the machiya's tiny courtyard garden, by the restroom.

kyoto_kissa_chianti_anekoji.notes: [Kissa · Karasuma-Oike] A long-established-feeling kissa with manga and smokers that packs out at lunch for its ¥1,000 daily plate — kara-age, Scotch egg or cutlet with a crowd of homemade sides and plenty of rice. Weekdays only; smoking allowed.

anecdotes.text: An October 2026 regular, back after a while, asks for less rice and still finds the ¥1,000 Scotch-egg plate more than enough.
A May 2026 walker drawn by a "service lunch ¥1,000" sign got the last counter seat for sweet-spicy fried chicken.

kyoto_nikudokoro_oota_ebisugawa.notes: [Yakiniku · Ebisugawa] A clean, calm yakiniku with charcoal grills in the counter and celebrity signatures on the wall: black wagyu tongue, whiteboard brand cuts, offal and an oxtail steam, plus Thursday–Friday lunches. Cash only; about ¥8,000–15,000.

chef_bio.background: Many celebrity autographs on the walls (November 2025 review).

anecdotes.text: An October 2026 regular says the steamed oxtail here beats every other version tried, alongside the tongue and crunchy horumon.
A May 2025 diner caught the Thursday–Friday-only lunch for a stone-pot bibimbap set behind three people already waiting.

kyoto_new_oriental_gojo.notes: [Taiwanese soups · Gojo] The Kyoto sister of Tokyo's SPICE Hanten, down an alley near Gojo: clear, gentle Taiwanese steamed soups with spiced small dishes and natural wine, open from the morning — a soothing stop. About ¥1,000–2,000.

chef_bio.background: Opened in November 2025 (Tabelog: 21 November 2025) as the second shop of the Nishi-Ogikubo restaurant SPICE Hanten in Tokyo (2025–26 reviews).

anecdotes.text: A February 2026 late-lunch guest had the jentan of Kyoto chicken and pork ribs with lily buds and found the clear broth gently salted but deep.
A December 2025 visitor at 10:45 on a Thursday took the peanut-shaped chopstick rest for ceramic until the staff said it could be eaten too.

kyoto_teuchi_soba_saka_gojozaka.vegan_detail: Not vegan: dashi broth, chirimen rice, herring and meat soba (2025–26 reviews).

On the right going up Gojo-zaka toward Kiyomizu-dera, about 10 min up the slope (Tabelog).
kyoto_teuchi_soba_saka_gojozaka.notes: [Soba · Gojo-zaka] A calm, wood-lined hand-made soba shop on the way up to Kiyomizu-dera, loved by locals and visitors: firm, smooth soba and freshly fried tempura, every set with a little rice bowl. About ¥1,000–2,000; lunch only.

chef_bio.background: Hand-made noodles; many regulars as well as tourists (May 2025 review).

anecdotes.text: An August 2025 driver stuck in a 2½-hour parking queue below Kiyomizu chose it for the ¥1,500 tempura soba — with rice — and found the vegetable tempura superb.
A November 2025 cold-soba fan tried nishin soba for the first time, for the occasion, and was won over by the broth.

kyoto_tominokoji_rest_house.hours_raw: Daily 9:00–16:30; closed over the New Year holidays; occasional closures for facility inspections (fng.or.jp, operator). kyoto_tominokoji_rest_house.notes: [Café · Kyoto Gyoen] A spacious, wood-furnished rest house in the Imperial Park by the tennis courts — a break between palace visits, with quiche, a cake set and outdoor tables for autumn leaves, plus souvenirs. Open daily; cards.

roles: Operator: 一般財団法人国民公園協会 (National Gardens Association)
chef_bio.background: A rest house run by the National Gardens Association, which manages visitor facilities in Kyoto Gyoen under the Ministry of the Environment’s Kyoto Gyoen office; it sits beside the Tominokoji plaza and tennis courts (fng.or.jp).

anecdotes.text: A September 2026 walker, tired after sightseeing, had a quiche with vegetables and soup and eyed the ¥1,500 cake set.
In July 2017 a rain-soaked pair fleeing a downpour after the Sento Palace tour warmed up with kitsune udon here.
A March 2019 visitor at a Kyoto Gosho special viewing liked the spacious, wooden room with matching tables and chairs.

kyoto_focacceria_chucho.gf_detail: Ask. The menu centres on focaccia sandwiches, cream puffs and banana bread, all wheat-based; no gluten information (September–November 2026 reviews).
kyoto_focacceria_chucho.vegan_detail: Ask. Sandwiches feature ham, chicken, duck and Parmesan; no vegan option mentioned (September–November 2026 reviews).

No service charge (Tabelog original なし). Non-smoking; English menu; kids menu (Tabelog). Opened 8 April 2026 (Tabelog). On Kinudana-dori just off Ebisugawa-dori, about 4–5 min walk from Marutamachi Stn (Tabelog; September 2026).
kyoto_focacceria_chucho.notes: [Café · near Marutamachi, from 8:30] A bright, stylish focaccia café from the COYOTE coffee team: chewy focaccia packed with homemade ham and tomato-almond sauce, a free second coffee with every set, and weekend fig cream puffs. Cashless; closed Tuesday.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviewers: opened 8 April 2026 on Kinudana-dori as a new concept from the popular Kyoto coffee shop COYOTE, with focaccia that tastes freshly baked in the shop (Tabelog; September–November 2026).

anecdotes.text: An October 2026 regular, rarely impressed by sandwiches, was won over by the focaccia and the homemade roast ham.
A September 2026 visitor came the very day the fig and tea cream puffs launched, and ordered the chai again.
A November 2026 holiday visitor arrived around 9 a.m. to two customers ahead and a relaxed room.

kyoto_morioka_kumano.gf_detail: Ask. Pasta is the mainstay; daily set meals such as roast pork or steak with rice may suit, but sauces are unknown; no gluten information (2017–2026 reviews).
kyoto_morioka_kumano.vegan_detail: Ask. Pastas include carbonara and bacon, sets centre on meat, and the pudding uses eggs and milk; no vegan information (2017–2026 reviews).
kyoto_morioka_kumano.hours_raw: Monday–Saturday 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–24:00; closed Sunday, though it may open by reservation (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Payment methods and service charge not listed on Tabelog. 10 seats; designated area for heated tobacco only (Tabelog). On the second floor at the back of the Palestate Nissei building opposite Kumano Shrine, by the Kumano Jinja-mae bus stop, 7 min walk from Jingu-Marutamachi Stn; look for a line-drawn sign (Tabelog; May 2023; November 2025; February 2026). Opened 7 November 2010 (Tabelog).
kyoto_morioka_kumano.notes: [Pasta and set meals · opposite Kumano Shrine, open late] A hidden ten-seat spot upstairs in a building by Kumano Shrine: generous carbonara sized by the 100 g, daily set meals and a homemade pudding to finish, at student prices. Gruff manner, good food. Closed Sunday.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog and reviewers: open since November 2010 at the back of a multi-tenant building opposite Kumano Shrine, serving pasta and daily set meals at low prices; reviewers describe the owner as brusque but a craftsman whose food is genuinely good (March 2024; February 2026).

anecdotes.text: A February 2026 regular found the owner intimidating at first but the pasta exceptional, and has grown to love the place.
A November 2025 lunch guest had pasta with salad and found the homemade pudding incredibly good.
In May 2023 a hungry traveller arrived to find the rice gone; the roast pork came without it, at a discount.
